docstring:
Continuous NACA four-digit geometry for the SBO experiment.

Inputs use unit-chord coordinates. The profile runs upper TE -> LE -> lower
TE, keeping a single LE and both finite-thickness TE endpoints. No model-number
rounding, coordinate clipping, or XFOIL re-paneling takes place here.

Formula reference: NASA TM-4741,
https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19970008124/downloads/19970008124.pdf

Typical use (YAML loading belongs to the caller)::

    result = generate_from_config(config, design=(0.0237, 0.436))
    write_airfoil(result, attempt_dir / "airfoil.dat")

Only NumPy and the Python standard library are required.

functions.name: check_geometry
functions.docstring:
Check a finite-TE contour, including its implicit closing TE segment.

A continuous contour here means a simple, nondegenerate, counterclockwise
polygon with nonzero neighboring edges. Nonadjacent touches and collinear
overlaps count as intersections. Neighboring segments may only share their
common endpoint. No x-monotonicity or [0, 1] clipping requirement is imposed.
calls: (np.maximum(np.minimum(q[i], ends[i]), np.minimum(q[j], ends[j])) <= np.minimum(np.maximum(q[i], ends[i]), np.maximum(q[j], ends[j])) + tolerance).all

docstring:
Read and validate XFOIL polar output without changing experiment data.

Use ``parse_attempt(attempt, config)`` after xfoil_runner.run_xfoil. Lower-level
text/file APIs support offline diagnostics and regression fixtures. Only a
``success`` result is usable for training; ``needs_review`` retains the measured
point but requires the evaluator's explicit human-review event.

Headers determine column positions. No fixed line skip or last-row assumption is
used. A valid target must match the final solve in the log, including viscous
mode and a save-file write. XFOIL 6.99 xoper.f calls PLRADD only when LVCONV is
true in viscous mode; xpol.f emits that write marker. MRCHDU warnings during
iterations do not by themselves invalidate a later converged solution.

Solver source: tools/xfoil/Xfoil699src.zip, Xfoil699src/src/{xoper,xpol}.f.
This parser verifies attempt-local artifacts, not database/cache provenance or
the baseline/final panel-convergence gates, which belong to the evaluator.

docstring:
One isolated XFOIL process per attempt, with bounded execution and audit files.

Example::

    settings = XfoilSettings.from_config(config, attempt_number=1)
    attempt = run_xfoil(geometry, settings, attempt_directory)

``completed`` means normal process execution and matching solver diagnostics, not
a valid aerodynamic sample. polar.py/evaluator.py must check the target polar row,
CL tolerance, convergence and review flags. Retries, budgets and caching belong to
the evaluator; this module never launches an automatic second attempt.

Menu reference: https://web.mit.edu/drela/Public/web/xfoil/xfoil_doc.txt
The two PPAR exit blanks were checked against 6.99 GETPAN in xfoil.f.
Windows uses a kill-on-close job with a suspended initial process so every child
is contained before execution. POSIX uses a fresh process group. psutil records
process identities and provides additional cleanup diagnostics.

functions.name: run_xfoil
functions.signature: geometry: Any, settings: XfoilSettings, attempt_dir: str | Path, *, on_launch: Callable[[LaunchEvent], None] | None=None
functions.docstring:
Run exactly one attempt in a directory that must not already exist.

geometry is the checked GeometryResult from geometry.py. Existing directories
(even empty), non-ASCII working paths and missing executables fail before a
launch. ``on_launch`` lets the evaluator record a budget/identity event; it is
called once after creation and persistence of process.json, before resuming a
Windows process. A callback error or KeyboardInterrupt cleans up and re-raises.
Raw logs are streamed directly to disk, so verbose solver output cannot block
on an undrained pipe. process.json records lifecycle only; result.json is left
to the aerodynamic evaluator.
